RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Rapidly switching extension inputs or clearing an extension editor while manifest/gallery resolution is pending allowed the obsolete continuation to perform README filesystem/network I/O, Markdown rendering, and webview allocation because disposing the CTS did not cancel its token.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Obsolete extension details could continue loading and rendering after navigation or editor clear, adding avoidable I/O, CPU/GC work, and transient webview resources.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The added disposal sentinel is set whenever transientDisposables is cleared and is checked after each awaited gallery/manifest stage, so superseded or cleared renders return before loading README content, rendering Markdown, or allocating a stale webview.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base render path, transientDisposables.clear() disposes the registered CancellationTokenSource with its default dispose(false), and CancellationTokenSource.dispose(false) only disposes the token emitter without setting isCancellationRequested. Therefore the base checks at the blamed line and after getManifest do not stop a superseded render. The stale continuation reaches renderNavbar/onNavbarChange, which calls extension.getReadme (filesystem for installed extensions or gallery network for Marketplace extensions), renders Markdown, and can create a webview overlay. The added test explicitly exercises switching/clearing while a manifest is pending and requires that only the current extension's README is requested and no cleared extension README is requested.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Agent Customizations and select the Extensions section without opening an extension page
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing extensions widget and tree are created when the contributed section first becomes visible. The new ExtensionEditor/page is not created and no page content is loaded until a row is explicitly opened, so the new heavyweight work is off this path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Installed extension count continues to control the existing tree render; the diff adds only bounded DOM, context-key, keybinding, and mouse listeners before first page use.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new asynchronous page work is scheduled on section entry. Existing marketplace search/render scheduling is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The page is absent on cold section entry and is retained for reuse only after first explicit page open. Existing marketplace and row caches are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: openExtensionPage is the only constructor site for AgentsWindowExtensionPage and guards creation with if (!this.page).
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact construction cost of the added back-button/context wiring is not measured, but it is constant and contains no expensive boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; the expensive editor and webview path is correctly lazy.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an installed or Marketplace extension page from a list row
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The click/Enter path lazily creates ExtensionEditor, resolves the selected manifest, loads the default Details/README content, renders Markdown, creates one webview overlay, and lays it out before full details are usable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the installed extension README via fileService.readFile when a local README URL is available.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one README read for the active Details render; ExtensionEditor Cache coalesces consumers within that render.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The Agents extension list had no extension-page workflow, so clicking a row did not load its README here.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The README read and Markdown render are on the page-content critical path, while the header can render around the manifest stage.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch a Marketplace extension manifest and README from the gallery when they are not local/cached.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One manifest and one README for the explicitly opened extension. Manifest requests are cached/coalesced in galleryResourcesCache and are often warm because Marketplace row warning rendering already requested the same manifest.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The list already fetched manifests for rendered Marketplace warning checks, but did not fetch README content or show a details webview.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A cold manifest gates navbar/content setup and a cold README gates the Details webview body.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Render extension Markdown and allocate one webview overlay for the selected tab.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One active content webview; switching, clearing, or leaving disposes the prior content store.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No extension details webview existed in this section.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On the page-content critical path after README retrieval.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One explicitly selected extension, with README size controlling Markdown CPU/allocation. The work does not fan out over the result list.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One page/editor instance per section widget and one active input. Superseded render continuations are now stopped by the added disposal sentinel; tab content cancellation disposes with cancel=true.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Installed manifests are in-memory. Marketplace manifests use the extension model's positive promise cache with deletion on failure; README content is cached for the current editor render but is reloaded after clearing/reopening. There is no negative-cache regression introduced here.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the call path from onDidOpen/openExtensionPage through show/setInput/render/openDetails is explicit, and the file/network implementations were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: README size and cold gallery/file latency vary, but the cardinality and lifecycle are bounded to the user-selected extension.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; this is the intentional, user-triggered cost of the new details feature, with lazy construction, manifest coalescing, and active-content cleanup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Navigate from an extension page to a dependency/publisher, or install/uninstall from the page
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Dependency navigation resolves an installed identifier in memory or performs one gallery lookup, then replaces the current input. Publisher/category navigation closes the page and enters the existing debounced Marketplace search. Install/uninstall waits for the existing extension management operation and then updates the section.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve a dependency identifier through extensionsWorkbenchService.getExtensions when it is not installed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One gallery lookup for the single dependency the user activates; installed dependencies require no boundary. User navigation is sequential rather than a loop over all dependencies.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This section could not navigate extension-page dependency links.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The lookup gates opening that dependency's page.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the existing debounced Marketplace query after a page publisher/category link requests a search.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced query for the final search text after the existing delayer; results are grouped once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same search boundary already ran for text entered in the section search box; the diff adds a page-link entry path to it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The page closes immediately; remote results arrive asynchronously on the list path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install or uninstall one selected extension through the existing extensions workbench/management service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One operation per explicit action, subject to existing action state and confirmation; extension packs/dependencies may be handled internally by the authoritative service rather than by a new per-item loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Equivalent install/uninstall operations were available from list-row controls; the diff adds the same operation from the details page without increasing per-action cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The action completion gates the page's installed/uninstalled state and enablement notification.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One activated dependency, one final search query, or one selected extension action. No changed loop fans these boundaries out over dependencies, search results, or installed extensions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Navigation replaces the single active editor input; rapid supersession is guarded after awaited stages. Search is delayed/coalesced. Install/uninstall concurrency remains controlled by existing actions/services.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Installed lookup is warm in the local array; gallery resolution and manifest retrieval use underlying service caches. Search uses the existing debounce/result state. No new retained per-identifier map is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: wrapper delegation and existing service implementations establish the boundary and cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote latency and extension-pack side effects vary, but the diff's effective boundary cardinality remains one per user action.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable fan-out or concurrency regression; the new entry points reuse authoritative operations with bounded user-driven cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Close a page, leave the Extensions section, switch harnesses, or clear the customization editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: closeExtensionPage clears the ExtensionEditor input, cancels current page show work, disposes active webviews, and returns to the list. Section replacement/removal disposes the widget through DisposableStore.delete, which also disposes window listeners, command registration, child services, and any cached page/editor.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One page/editor per live Extensions section widget; resources do not accumulate across repeated page opens or harness-driven widget replacement.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each show cancels the previous page-level source; ExtensionEditor disposal sentinels prevent superseded manifest continuations from reaching README/Markdown/webview work. No cleanup queue or burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The page shell is reused while the widget remains live, but active input/webview caches are cleared on page close. Full widget disposal releases the retained shell and listeners.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: clearInput clears both content and transient stores, and the parent replacement path calls DisposableStore.delete, whose implementation disposes the child store/widget.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The retained editor shell size between page close and widget disposal is unmeasured, but it is a single bounded instance created only after use.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable cleanup or retention regression. The PR also fixes a pre-existing stale-render path that could perform obsolete README I/O, Markdown rendering, and webview allocation; that fix was recorded through report_regression_fix.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete 15-file diff and traced startup/section creation, page opening, dependency/search/action navigation, rendering/layout, caches, concurrency, and disposal. No high-confidence performance regression was introduced. The shared ExtensionEditor disposal-sentinel change fixes a concrete pre-existing obsolete-render performance mechanism and was recorded separately.
